status: Same frozen selector extended to the existing pair-free prediction artifacts after the pair screen passed its follow-up gate
selector: Largest mean symmetric pairwise CA lDDT to the other two samples; 15 A neighborhoods; errors strictly below 0.5, 1, 2, 4 A; first sample wins exact ties
inputs: Predicted CA coordinates only. No native coordinates, model-native scores, or fitted coefficients enter selection.
evaluation: All 626 development targets; paired sequence-cluster bootstrap against both fixed first sample and mean across samples, with CA lDDT and geometry reported separately
oracle: Native-TM best-of-three is a diagnostic upper bound only, never a deployable policy
followup_gate: Consider a second untouched checkpoint or independent inference-noise replication only if mean TM gain over random-sample expectation is at least 0.002, its 95% sequence-cluster interval is above zero, and first-sample TM and mean CA lDDT do not regress
cost: No GPU allocation. Existing three-sample pair-free predictions only. Any end-to-end speed or memory claim requires a complete sequence-to-structure benchmark with the chosen policy.
limitations: CA lDDT is insensitive to chirality and does not guarantee native correctness; agreement among three correlated errors can select a wrong structure. Selection and geometry must be reported without oracle substitution.
final_test: Keep the 34 locked targets unscored. This diagnostic does not replace the accuracy-promotion gate.
comparison: Within pair-free: chosen versus sample mean and fixed first sample. Separately compare selected pair-free with selected pair model. Different trained checkpoints prevent a causal architectural claim.
